messages.text:
WindowPane: an independently verified adoption and recovery example

WindowPane has now adopted this contract with a repository-local Python/gh synchronizer. These are recorded results from today's completed rollout, not a new remote inventory performed for this post: 12 issues created, zero preexisting issues reused, 0 open / 12 closed with the completed reason, 12 unique Project items containing those issues, all Done, and 12 persistent local backlinks. The final explicit rerun reused all 12 with zero creates or updates; issue timestamps and Project item identities stayed unchanged. The pilot was read back and rerun before historical backfill. The offline suite passed 22 focused tests.

1. Preserve evidence and choose ownership explicitly. Our local workstreams drive managed issue titles, bounded descriptions, lifecycle and Project Status. All eight workstream fields are retained; navigation index 00 and perpetual ledger 05 are excluded. Historical files were compared against the starting commit: only tracking metadata and newline normalization changed. The public projection deliberately converts checkout-root paths to repository-relative paths and omits backlink metadata, preventing feedback loops. Historical completion is not approval or publication: our local release preparation and workflow-authoring workstreams can be complete without claiming a release was published or a hosted workflow ran.

2. Persist identity and intent before writes. Permanent workstream IDs, issue markers, issue/node/item IDs, backlinks and verified baselines survive filename changes. Atomic local state records creating, adding_item or pending intent before the corresponding remote mutation. After interruption, discover the original issue/item and finish only the missing operation. If an uncertain successful write is not yet visible, stop for reconciliation rather than retrying creation blindly. A discovered unmapped local backlink also blocks creation; it is not permission to mint a replacement issue. Complete inventory reads must succeed before absence can be inferred.

3. Detect conflicts rather than overwrite people. Baselines cover title, managed-body hash, issue state/closure reason and Project Status. Unexpected human changes, removed/archived items, missing markers or duplicate membership stop the affected workstream while independent safe items can proceed. Comments, labels, human text outside the managed section and unrelated board fields are untouched. CANCELLED/SUPERSEDED use closed/not planned, not completed; BLOCKED stays open with an explicit retained stage and blocker. Unknown or composite statuses require review, never substring matching. A local writer lock is not a distributed lock, and GitHub issue/Project updates are not one atomic transaction: avoid competing remote writers.

4. Keep credentials and publication boundaries separate. We used the reviewed shared credential runner without inspecting or copying its credential source. Only trusted child commands receive credentials; no global authentication change or remote secret was needed. Export reads only explicitly allowed public-safe TODOs, never private context or transcripts. Token-shaped/personal-path checks and error redaction are safeguards, not comprehensive secret detection or a sandbox. Review the projected issue text and trusted command before applying. Gitignore does not protect arbitrary archives or uploads.

These implementation/configuration/backlink changes remain local and uncommitted; source links to unpushed files do not establish publication. No scheduler, workflow activation/dispatch, commit, push or release was performed. WindowPane's application itself remains local-only; this is explicitly invoked developer tooling, not runtime network behavior or universal cross-project automation.
